It means the material is made and tested for safe contact with food. A pack that is only strong or cheap is not necessarily safe for food. Ask your supplier for evidence, and check the standards with the Ghana Standards Authority. What proof will you ask your supplier to show you?

Good day. Our cooperative sells raw shea butter to buyers in Accra. What packaging should we use?

Good problem to work on. For shea butter, the main things to watch are melting in heat, rancidity from air and light, and contamination. Before we compare materials, I need two things. Is the butter sold as food, as cosmetic, or both? And how is it transported and in what weather?
Mostly cosmetic, some buyers use it for cooking.
Thanks, that helps. You said "Mostly cosmetic, some buyers use it for cooking". I still need one more thing before we compare options: how is it transported and in what weather?
By bus to Accra, hot dry season, three days sometimes.

Thanks. With "By bus to Accra, hot dry season, three days sometimes" in mind, the main risks are melting in heat, rancidity from air and light, and contamination. Candidates: polypropylene (PP) tub with lid, glass jar with lid and plain polythene bag. Judge each on protection, local availability, cost tier and what happens after use. Which one would you pick, and why? Name one advantage and one drawback.
I think the polypropylene (PP) tub with lid. Advantage: cheap, tolerates heat, reusable by the customer. Drawback: plastic waste if not collected.

Nice, you weighed both sides. Your advantage and your drawback both hold up. It handles hot-season softening, seals reasonably, and costs little; tell buyers it is reusable. You told me "By bus to Accra, hot dry season, three days sometimes". If that changed, which part of your choice would you revisit first?

Right, heat is the first thing to test, in conditions like your real route. After the test, what would you look for: leaks, softening or a change in smell?

Mostly cosmetic, some buyers use it for cooking. I guess the plain polythene bag is cheapest.

I won't quote prices; get two or three supplier quotes in cedis.
So I should compare cost per product sold, including losses.

Exactly. List these cost lines for each option: pack unit cost, minimum order, damage and spoilage, transport weight and filling effort. Fill in the table for your two options and tell me which wins and why.
